key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this does not translate into better high-angle erosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coating design, axial-fed HV-APS is a strong upgrade path when hardness and sliding wear matter, while erosion performance may remain unchanged under 90° impact.
method: Compared Cr3C2–NiCr coatings deposited on S235 steel by conventional APS with radial powder injection and by HV-APS with axial powder feeding.
Characterized microstructure, phase composition, hardness, porosity, erosion behavior, and ball-on-disc tribological wear.
Assessed how spray technology alters carbide retention, solid-solution formation, and damage mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, increased microhardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and lowered tribological wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3, while erosion rates stayed nearly identical at 0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g.
watch_item: Improved density and hardness did not improve erosion at 90° impact, so process selection should match the dominant service wear mode.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
